Definition: neuter of G2413; a sacred place, i.e. the entire precincts (whereas G3485 denotes the central sanctuary itself) of the Temple (at Jerusalem or elsewhere):--temple.
BiblicalUsage: Hierón is the temple — the sacred place itself, not the word for “holy”. The form stands 20 times in the Greek New Testament, and 19 of them are the temple: Matthew, Luke and Acts show it in use.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hierón matters because the temple is where God met His people, and the word for the place is worth knowing.
RelatedEvents: The Cleansing of the Temple; The Presentation of Jesus in the Temple; Peter Heals the Lame Man
